data.name: Harikrishna
data.gender_notes: Harikrishna is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.short_meaning: Hari (God Vishnu) + Krishna (Darkness, Absence of Illusion)
data.long_meaning: Harikrishna is a combination of two powerful Sanskrit words: Hari and Krishna. Hari refers to Lord Vishnu, the preserver of the universe. Krishna refers to the all-pervading darkness or the absence of illusion. Thus, Harikrishna signifies the divine presence that transcends both illusion and reality. It is a name deeply rooted in Hindu mythology and spirituality.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of divine presence and inner wisdom.
data.etymology: Harikrishna belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Hari (God Vishnu) + Krishna (Darkness, Absence of Illusion).”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Harikrishna total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

data.cultural_impact: Harikrishna is a revered name in Hinduism, evoking deep devotion and awe. Its usage is common in various religious practices and texts. The name captures the essence of the belief in Lord Vishnu, who is believed to protect his followers and maintain the cosmic order. Harikrishna is often chanted in mantras and hymns, adding a spiritual dimension to daily life.
data.spiritual_significance: Harikrishna's significance lies at the core of Hindu philosophy, emphasizing the reality beyond the physical world. The name signifies a reminder to seek the divine presence that exists beyond the veil of illusion. It calls for the meditation on the truth of consciousness, detachment from worldly pleasures, and a constant reminder of the ultimate goal of spiritual growth - union with God.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Harikrishna signifies the divine merge of Hari (Vishnu) and Krishna within an individual, symbolizing the attainment of pure love, devotion, and consciousness towards the supreme being.

historical_references.reference: Harikrishna was a prominent leader during the Satavahana dynasty, ruling from the 1st century BCE to the 3rd century CE. His name is mentioned in several inscriptions, one of which states that he was a 'great king' who vanquished his enemies and expanded his kingdom.

Harikrishna was also a notable Jainism teacher and philosopher, who lived around the 8th century CE. He is known for his commentary on the Agama texts and his philosophy on the nature of the soul and the attainment of spiritual liberation.

modern_usage.modern_context: In today's interconnected world, the name Harikrishna continues to be cherished by Hindu families globally. It is frequently featured on social media platforms where parents share their naming journeys, and Hindu name websites where expectant parents research meaningful names. The name bridges traditional Hindu values with modern Indian identity, making it relevant for contemporary families seeking names with deep spiritual and cultural significance.
